meta.notes: Initial structure and watchlist. Numeric values are directional placeholders until the first dated ingestion pass. Replace observations in this file without changing the UI.

layers.title: Machine activity
layers.description: Are autonomous systems creating more requests, tool calls, data movement, traces, and machine-to-machine communication?

layers.title: Enterprise adoption & control
layers.description: Are enterprises moving from demos to governed deployments with identity, permissions, observability, and policy controls?

layers.title: Company capture
layers.description: Which public companies convert agentic workload growth into durable revenue, margin, retention, or free-cash-flow improvement?

expectations.assumption: Consensus recognizes training and inference demand, but may underweight the second-order request, telemetry, security, and data footprint of agents.
Enterprise controls may become a budget line only after identity, data-loss, and agent-permission incidents become visible.
The application layer may retain the highest willingness-to-pay while infrastructure remains a cost center. This is the key counter-case.

breakers.title: Agents stay assistive, not operational
breakers.description: Usage grows, but humans remain in the loop for every meaningful action; machine actions per intent fail to compound.

breakers.title: Consumption is bundled away
breakers.description: Platforms absorb traffic, logs, and security events into flat-price products, preventing infrastructure vendors from capturing the activity.

breakers.title: Target companies miss the mix shift
breakers.description: Wave 2 grows, but workloads consolidate into hyperscaler-native services or accrue to companies outside the watchlist.
